clue.text: To enlarge, factory needs show of figures

parts.note: to wax is to grow larger, as the moon does
works is a word for a factory or plant

explanation.surface: A factory is told it needs a display of sales figures to expand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show of figures' reads like statistics, but it means an exhibition of modelled human figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A waxworks is an exhibition of lifelike modelled people, such as Madame Tussauds.

clue.text: Rainy? Everybody inside in that case

indicators.note: inside means one word goes within another

parts.note: rainy weather is wet
all means everybody

explanation.surface: In wet weather, everybody stays indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rainy?' looks like a weather question; it gives the synonym that 'inside' opens up, and 'in that' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a small folding case for money and cards.

clue.text: English phone-box being out of order, one dreads overseas calls

indicators.note: being out of order means the letters are not in their proper sequence

explanation.surface: A broken telephone box frightens someone who needs to call abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' reads as a broken phone; it is the jumble signal. 'calls' is a nudge: such a person dreads foreign visits, not phone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A xenophobe fears or hates foreigners and so dreads trips abroad.

clue.text: But this in an animal's ear won't make it stone-deaf

definitions.text: But this in an animal's ear won't make it stone-deaf

parts.words: But this in an animal's ear won't make it stone-deaf
parts.note: a small stone in the inner ear helps balance and hearing, so a stone in the ear does not make the animal deaf

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is literal: 'stone-deaf' means fully deaf, yet a tiny stone really sits in the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An otolith is a calcium grain in the inner ear of vertebrates that senses gravity and motion.

clue.text: German conductor in quick Emperor section

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from the run of words, so the name lies within them

explanation.surface: A German maestro takes a fast passage of Beethoven's Emperor concerto.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolf Kempe was a German conductor, so the musical picture is apt; the letters run across quicK EMPEror.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Kempe was a German conductor, famed for Strauss and Wagner.

clue.text: Sadly miss church leaders in such a break?

indicators.note: in places the church's leading letters inside the jumble
sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the word miss is jumbled

parts.note: the two leading letters of church are C and H

explanation.surface: Someone regrets missing church leaders during a split in the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' signals the jumble and 'in' the insertion. The definition leans on the surface: a split among church leaders is the classic case.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division, especially within a church.

clue.text: Peculiar dialect of the Kremlin, for example

indicators.note: peculiar means strange or odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd way of speaking is heard inside the Kremlin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortress at the heart of Moscow, a classic example of a fortified stronghold.

clue.text: Standard of Euclid's fifth proposition accepted

indicators.note: fifth picks the letter in fifth place of the word

parts.note: a deal is an offer or proposition that has been agreed

explanation.surface: Euclid's fifth proposition is accepted as the standard of geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: Euclid's fifth postulate is famous, which makes 'fifth proposition' look geometric; it is the fifth letter of Euclid.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of perfection to aim at.

clue.text: Quickly styled in Windsor, this motorway pressure

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, written MI in crosswords
stress means pressure or strain

explanation.surface: A rushed hairdo in Windsor, under motorway pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Mistress Quickly is a character in Shakespeare's The Merry Wives of Windsor; 'styled' means titled, not coiffed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress Quickly is the hostess in Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor, so this title goes with that surname.

clue.text: Branch cricket-side taking bag

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field, opposite the leg side
to bag game is to shoot it

explanation.surface: A branch of a cricket club takes in a kit bag.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side. 'bag' is a verb: hunters bag birds by shooting them.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side growth from a plant, or a branch of an organisation.

clue.text: Maybe Taft's harmony led in it

definitions.text: Maybe Taft's harmony led in it

indicators.note: maybe hints the letters could be arranged otherwise, signalling a jumble

parts.note: Taff is a nickname for a Welshman; with the s it gives TAFFS

explanation.surface: A Welshman's harmonies lead the singing of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: TAFFS, HARMONY and LED rearranged give the title; the whole clue also describes Welsh voices leading the national anthem in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Land of My Fathers is the English title of Wales's national anthem, sung heartily by Welsh crowds.

clue.text: Exposed to capture like a man on board

explanation.surface: A board-game piece is left vulnerable to being taken.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a piece left open to being taken is described as en prise; a chessman on the board can be in that state.

clue.text: One up in his product

parts.note: a rider sits up in the leather seat that this craftsman makes

explanation.walkthrough: 'One up' sounds like being ahead in a contest, but it is a rider mounted on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler is a craftsman who makes the seats riders sit on horseback.

clue.text: Reluctant to touch a foreign flower? Here's a rake

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant
a flower is something that flows, a river; Rio is Spanish and Portuguese for river

explanation.surface: Someone shy of touching an exotic bloom turns out to be a gardener's rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword trick for a river (it flows), and 'foreign' asks for a non-English word, RIO. 'to touch' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, as is a rake, after the character in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: Extremely hot, trio sang raggedly

indicators.note: raggedly means untidily, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Three singers perform badly in sweltering heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting describes heat fierce enough to cook in, a sweltering day.

clue.text: Classic place to find a tail-less insect

indicators.note: tail-less means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a locust is a swarming grasshopper

explanation.surface: A guide says where one can find an insect without a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' here means classical, Latin: locus is the Latin word for place.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for a place or position, used in English for a site or centre.

clue.text: Pink in motor-race

parts.note: a motor is a car
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Someone is in the pink at a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like the contest; here it is a people, a nation. 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink is a garden flower of the dianthus family, the group that includes the carnation.

clue.text: Bounty, tidy ship going east

parts.note: a tidy sum is a large one
SS stands for steamship
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A neat vessel sails east, as the Bounty might have.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bounty was a famous ship, but here bounty is generosity. 'tidy' means sizeable, as in a tidy sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving, a bounty of gifts or money.

clue.text: Hebrew character going cast in the sacred river

indicators.note: in places the compass letter inside the river's name

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A Hebrew figure travels east along a holy river.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Kubla Khan opens with 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

clue.text: Clyde, for instance, needs cowl over chimney

indicators.note: over means the first piece sits above the second in this down entry

parts.note: a cowl is a hood
lum is a Scots and northern word for chimney

explanation.surface: A Scottish river needs a cowl placed over a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: Clyde suggests the Scottish river, which fits Scots LUM; here it is Clyde Barrow, the gangster of Bonnie and Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Clyde Barrow was an American gangster, a classic thug.

clue.text: Self-banking aircraft?

parts.note: auto- is the prefix meaning self
giro is a system of bank transfers, as in the British National Giro

explanation.surface: A plane that can bank itself, or one that banks on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-banking' reads as an aircraft tilting by itself into a turn; banking here is the money sense, a giro.
explanation.definitionFit: An autogiro is a rotorcraft whose unpowered rotor gives lift while a propeller drives it forward.

clue.text: Marx whose complaint came to nothing

parts.note: a grouch is a grumble or complaint
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Marx brother whose complaint came to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Marx could be Karl, but here it is Groucho of the Marx Brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was the moustached, cigar-wielding Marx brother of film comedy.

clue.text: VIP's the big one on the board

definitions.text: VIP's the big one on the board

parts.words: VIP's the big one on the board
parts.note: an important person is called the big wheel of some kind, and the board may be a company board or a platter served after dinner

explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a company board of directors, where VIPs sit; it is a board of food served at the end of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is a slang term for an important person, and a dairy selection is served on a board.

clue.text: Kind of diplomacy requiring craft in the main

explanation.surface: A style of statecraft that relies on ships at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunboat diplomacy means backing policy with naval threat, and a gunboat is a small warship on the main, the open sea.

clue.text: Orderly over hospital in South Wales

indicators.note: over means the first piece sits above the second in this down entry

parts.note: neat means tidy or orderly
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly works in South Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital porter; it is an adjective meaning tidy. The definition names the place by where it lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a town near Swansea, in the south of Wales.

clue.text: Tolerate the military marches on it

explanation.surface: Soldiers have to put up with marching on an empty belly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to put up with it, and an army marches on its belly, as the saying credited to Napoleon goes.

clue.text: Frenchman caught by divers in the river

indicators.note: caught by means held inside another word

parts.note: divers is an old word for various or some
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is pulled from the river by divers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' reads as underwater swimmers; it is the archaic adjective meaning several.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is the river in northern France famed for the 1916 battle.

clue.text: Can impale things anyhow in the office

definitions.text: Can impale things anyhow in the office

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A desk device that can pierce paperwork any old way.
explanation.definitionFit: A stapler drives metal wire through sheets of paper, an everyday desk tool.

clue.text: Formerly part of Manchester, we hear, opposite to Bury?

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: we hear signals that the district's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Hulme is an inner-city district of Manchester

explanation.surface: An area once in Manchester is said to be across from the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, which makes 'opposite' look geographical; here bury is the verb, and its opposite is digging up.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig a body out of the grave, undoing a burial.

clue.text: Condemn blockhead knocking one back inside

indicators.note: inside places the turned word within the blockhead

parts.note: a dunce is a slow or stupid person

indicators.note: back means the word one is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a fool for knocking back a drink indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking one back' sounds like downing a drink; 'back' is the reversal signal and 'inside' the insertion, with 'knocking' only colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to publicly criticise or accuse.
